bug_semantics: During Linux container creation, image configuration processing calls WithAdditionalGIDs for the configured UID or for root. A malicious image can supply an /etc/group containing arbitrarily many entries whose member lists include that user. user.ParseGroupFileFilter/ParseGroupFilter retains every matching Group, and containerd then materializes every matching GID, with no total file-size or entry-count bound. The resulting allocations exhaust containerd's memory, OOM-kill the daemon, and make the runtime API unavailable.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism originated in containerd commit 78e61af47a3f5d539b405b39a7230c99369639bc, which added WithAdditionalGIDs and getSupplementalGroupsFromPath in oci/spec_opts.go. The new helper passed image-rootfs /etc/group to user.ParseGroupFileFilter with a broad membership predicate, retained all matching Group objects, and copied all matching GIDs without bounding total input. Commit 13931e41d62cea69a571e8d8a44d8981deffdc5d later wired that already-flawed helper into WithImageConfigArgs by default for both configured users and root; it activated the normal image-creation path but did not first write the vulnerable parser/accumulator. The generic user parser is an enabling dependency, while the containerd BIC created the attacker-reachable all-supplemental-groups accumulation.

The advisory's normal attack path consists of image-config processing, default invocation of WithAdditionalGIDs, parsing image-controlled /etc/group, retention of every group matching the selected user, and a second allocation for the resulting GIDs. Commit 78e61af47a3f5d539b405b39a7230c99369639bc is the smallest causal commit because it first added both the broad-match supplemental-group API and its unbounded parser/accumulator; its immediate parent contains neither. Commit 13931e41d62cea69a571e8d8a44d8981deffdc5d is important later activation evidence but is not the first writer of the flawed mechanism, and 19735b55a813d69a867d9917479028d46b0b4a32 is explicitly a release/1.1 backport. The BIC is ancestral to every advisory lower-bound tag. The canonical fix 7b05ec421d0a07b33964c74145b6bf5dff58f476 bounds all user-database reads to 10 MiB and rejects non-regular inputs, with equivalent direct backports present exactly in each advertised patched tag and absent from each preceding vulnerable tag. Finally, the raw BIC commit object has only human author/committer identity and a human Signed-off-by trailer. The AI marker on the 2026 fix cannot retroactively attribute the 2018 BIC, so the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
